description: Cross-language vector for what a receiver admits on the two decline paths (Sections 7.5 and 7.6). Both suites build the same session: an initiator's signed round-1 offer at sequence_number 1 has been processed, the session is NEGOTIATING, and the responder then sends the act below through the state machine. Every case starts from a fresh session. Keys are generated by each suite and are not part of the vector.

signature_presence.description: A decline's signature is OPTIONAL, but a signature that is present is always checked. Each case places signature in the act's signature field when the case carries a signature member, and removes the field when it does not. Only an absent field is the unsigned act, accepted and later recorded as an unsigned observation. A present field is a signature claim whatever its value, and is refused when it does not verify: a null, empty or non-string value is refused outright, and it is never read as unsigned. The published schemas refuse the same values.

withdrawal_round_number.description: round_number is REQUIRED on a Withdrawal (Section 7.6) because it is part of the common header every signed act covers, and the schema requires it unconditionally. The runtime and withdrawal.schema.json must reach the same verdict on every case: schema_valid and accepted are always equal. Each case sets round_number on the withdrawal act when the case carries a round_number member and removes it when it does not, and is run twice: once unsigned, with sender_verification_method removed, and once signed by the responder's key over the act's rebuilt hash, or over a stand-in payload when the act does not rebuild. The verdict is the same both times, because the requirement does not depend on whether the act is signed. round_number is the round in progress, so a withdrawal sent before any offer carries 1. It is judged by value: 1.0 is the integer 1 and -0.0 the integer 0 in other JSON spellings, and a boolean is not a number.
